regions_game_px.name: far openings of the podlubie (bay 1 and, through the fence, bays 2-3)

instruction:
The picture shows the yard side of a 1970s Slovak housing-estate school in June 1995. Make one small local change in the right half of the picture.

Right of the entrance canopy (about 58-75 % from the left, 30-37 % from the top) the ground floor of the long building is an open covered passage ("podlubie") on square pillars. At its far end it now shows a bright glimpse of pale prefabricated panel blocks of flats and green trees. That is wrong: the passage only leads into the school's own small, enclosed inner courtyard. Replace that glimpse in every opening of the passage: behind the passage lies a small sunlit inner courtyard of the school - a strip of mown lawn and a few low shrubs on the ground - and close behind it the plain pale-yellowish rendered wall of another wing of the same school, with a row of the same white-framed windows as the main building and a darker band at its foot; this wall fills each far opening right up to the passage ceiling. No panel blocks of flats, no tall buildings, no sky and no distant trees in the openings. It must read as a closed little courtyard, not as a way through.

Keep everything else exactly as it is: the square pillars, the dark passage ceiling, the brown side wall of the passage, the passage floor, the entrance canopy and steps, the upper floors, and in front of the two right openings every post, rail and chain-link mesh panel of the dark-green court fence. No people, no text.

Image 2 is another background from the same game: keep the same painting technique.

parent_prompt:
Image 1 is one of our finished point-and-click adventure game backgrounds (painted, style A). Make exactly the local changes described below and change nothing else: keep every other object, the camera, the composition, all positions, sizes, colours and the light exactly as in image 1. No people, no animals, no cars, no text, no letters, no logos, no frames. The picture shows the yard side of a 1970s Slovak housing-estate school in June 1995. Make two local changes, both in the right half of the picture.

CHANGE 1 - lawn instead of the footpath. A grey paved footpath runs from the foot of the entrance steps (about 57 % from the left, 40 % from the top) diagonally down to the right along the LEFT side of the tall dark-green chain-link fence, and widens into a paved area right of the low red-brick wall. Remove this footpath completely. Its whole area, from the grass bank below the entrance down to the yard, becomes the same mown green lawn as the big lawn left of it (same grass colour, texture and light, a few longer tufts along the fence foot), reaching right up to the bottom rail of the fence. Towards the yard the new lawn ends in a straight low concrete kerb, the continuation of the kerb that edges the lawn at the left side of the picture: it runs level at about 59 % from the top, from behind the right end of the brick wall, behind the red pipe, to the fence behind the round steel dustbin. In front of that kerb the worn grey yard asphalt stays exactly as it is. The brick wall with its stone panel, the red pipe elbow, the dustbin and every fence post, rail and mesh panel stay exactly as they are. The short paved landing at the foot of the entrance steps and the path leading from it to the LEFT stay.

CHANGE 2 - an open underpass right of the entrance. Image 2 is a photo of the real place, taken in the 2020s when the ground floor had colourful murals: right of the glass entrance doors the ground floor of the long building is not a wall but an open covered passage straight through the building (a "podlubie") to the panel blocks of flats behind the school; the upper floors rest on a row of square pillars, the space between the pillars is open and the passage behind them is deep and dim. In image 1, the three ground-floor bays right of the entrance canopy - the brick lower walls and the windows between the cream pillars, from the canopy's right edge (about 58 % from the left) to the third pillar to its right (about 75 % from the left), between about 29 % and 37 % from the top - become such an open passage: keep the pillars, the pale band above them and all the upper floors exactly where they are; remove the brick and the windows between the pillars; show the dark shaded underside of the first floor as the passage ceiling, a few more pillars receding inside, the passage floor level with the entrance landing, and at the far end of the passage a small bright opening with a glimpse of the sunlit far side: pale prefabricated panel blocks of flats with rows of windows, and green trees. The pillars and the passage walls are plain pale yellowish render like the rest of the 1995 building - no murals, no paintings, no graffiti, no gates, no signs. Two of the three bays are seen through the court fence: keep every fence post, rail and mesh panel in front of them exactly as it is.

Image 3 is another background from the same game: keep the same painting technique. Style: classic 1990s hand-painted adventure game background. Rich painterly brushwork, slightly exaggerated cartoon proportions with gently curved lines, warm late-afternoon sunlight, saturated but harmonious colours, soft dappled shadows under the trees.
